paper.title: Bias, efficiency and consistency of ETS smoothing-parameter estimates: smooth vs statsforecast

declarations.competing_interests: Ivan Svetunkov, the guarantor and supervisor of this study, is the author of the smooth package, one of the two implementations compared. No other competing interests declared.

Series are simulated from the innovations form of ETS with additive Gaussian errors $\varepsilon_t \sim N(0,1)$, independent, starting from fixed states with no burn-in, for series lengths $T \in \{50,100,250,500\}$ and $R=300$ replicates per cell (process x parameters x $T$).
ETS(A,N,N): $$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + \alpha\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$ with $\alpha \in \{0.1, 0.5\}$.
ETS(A,A,N): $$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \alpha\varepsilon_t \\ b_t &= b_{t-1} + \beta\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$ with $(\alpha,\beta) \in \{(0.3,0.05),(0.5,0.2)\}$.
ETS(A,N,A), period $m=12$: $$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + s_{t-m} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + \alpha\varepsilon_t \\ s_t &= s_{t-m} + \gamma\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$ with $(\alpha,\gamma)=(0.2,0.1)$.
Initial states: $l_0=100$, $b_0=1$, $s_j = 10\sin(2\pi j/12)$ for $j=0,\dots,11$ ($s_0$ belongs to the first observation's season). Replicate seeds are SeedSequence([2026, process-set index, T, replicate]).

evidence.description: Single confirmatory simulation run (RN2, plan PL1) of 28,800 fit rows: R=300 replicates in each of 20 cells (five parameter sets of the simulation design x series lengths 50, 100, 250, 500), each series fitted by three arms with the model form fixed to the generating form (smooth with optimised initial states, smooth with backcasting, statsforecast), all by Gaussian likelihood. No fit failed in any arm. Per arm, cell and parameter the bias (with a 90% interval), RMSE, MAE, failures, bound hits and warned fits were computed over replicates and are in the results file (artefact A1); the tables give the quantities that decide the six hypotheses: T1 the shares of RMSE comparisons (32 process x parameter x T comparisons), T2 the largest upper and lower 90% bounds of the absolute bias over the eight parameters at T=500, per arm. Not reported in the tables, but in A1: an exploratory reading of A1 shows that all the bias beyond 0.02 at T=500 sits in the seasonal process (gamma for both smooth arms; alpha for statsforecast), read after the verdicts and not a planned test.

limitations.statement: Only five parameter sets (three process forms, one seasonal set) are simulated, so the bias results at T=500 describe these settings; the bias beyond 0.02 appears only in the single seasonal process, read from the results file after the verdicts.

Neither smooth nor statsforecast exposes a convergence flag that the script reads, so non-convergence is visible only as bound hits and warnings, which are counted; no fit raised an error, returned a non-finite estimate or changed the model form.

The bounds differ slightly between the packages (smooth: usual bounds; statsforecast: box [1e-4, 0.9999] plus usual and admissibility checks), and the optimisers differ, so differences in RMSE partly reflect these implementation choices.
The thresholds (bias bound 0.02, share 0.75) were fixed in advance without a prior literature basis and the consistency test compares only the smallest and the largest series length.
